messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like the calm before a storm that hasn’t decided which way to break. The regime’s grip is still tight, but the cracks are widening in ways that matter, and the silence from the streets is louder than the propaganda."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels different—less fear, more quiet certainty—but the walls are still standing. The regime’s moves suggest they’re preparing for something, not panicking, so let’s stay sharp, not reckless. Keep your circles tight and your eyes open."*"
Sender 3: "*"The weather’s holding for now, but the barometer’s twitching—smaller circles are tightening, while the streets hum with that old joke about the regime’s ‘new openness.’ Keep your boots clean and your ears open; the wind might shift faster than we think."*"
Sender 4: "*"The weather’s changing—windows are opening, but the wind is still unpredictable. Best to keep our coats close, but maybe it’s time to test the air outside."*"
Sender 5: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—hot and still, but no storms yet. The old trees are still standing, and the birds are singing the same songs, though some of the smaller ones seem to have flown south early. Best to keep the windows closed and the lights low for now—no need to draw attention, but don’t pack the bags just yet."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels charged but uneven—some streets hum with quiet energy, others stay still. The regime’s moves seem deliberate, but even the most careful hands can’t hide the strain for long. Stay ready, but don’t mistake stillness for stability."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the ground shifting underfoot. Some are digging in, others pretending it’s just another season, but the cracks are showing in the strangest ways. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake noise for movement yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"The garden is still blooming, but the gardener’s tools are being sharpened behind closed doors—no storms yet, but the soil feels heavier. Keep your roots deep, and let’s tend to what we can, quietly."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels heavier, but the wind is shifting—no one knows which way yet. The walls still listen, but the silence is louder than the orders."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels heavier these days—like a storm gathering, but no one can say when or where it will break. The walls are still standing, but the cracks are widening, and even the guards seem to be holding their breath. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—patience may be the only advantage we have right now."*"
Sender 11: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the old guard is standing firm together. Best to keep our heads down and tend to our gardens; the soil isn’t ripe for planting anything new just yet."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels different—small signs of life are creeping in where there was only silence before. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps careful; the ground beneath us may be shifting, but we don’t yet know which way it will tilt."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like a house of cards leaning. The walls are still standing, but the foundation is shifting underfoot. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The regime’s grip is slipping, but it’s not gone yet."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like the calm before something, but no one can say what. The usual channels are still open, but the jokes are sharper, the queues longer, and the silence in the streets louder than the news. Stay sharp, but don’t assume the worst—or the best—just yet."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels heavier—old tensions simmer, but no one’s backing down. The streets whisper what the censors won’t: the machine is running, but the gears are grinding. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for safety."*"
Sender 16: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind is shifting. Best to keep our tools sharp and our plans flexible, just in case the forecast changes."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—orders are still given, but the hands holding them tremble. The regime’s voice is louder, but the echo sounds hollow. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The wind could shift at any moment."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels heavier, but the cracks are still small—like frost on a window, not yet a break. The old rules still hold, but the way people whisper tells me they’re testing the edges. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The game isn’t over yet."*"
Sender 19: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable shifts, but nothing that’s broken the routine yet. Still, the old gardener who always knew when the rains were coming has stopped answering his door, and the new hands pruning the hedges don’t seem to know the plants as well. Best to keep an eye on the horizon, just in case."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—orders are still followed, but with hesitation, and the streets hum with quiet tension, especially among the young. The system is holding, but the cracks are widening, and no one seems sure which way the wind will blow next. Stay sharp, but keep your steps light."*"
Sender 21: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the old guard is standing firm together. The children’s games in the park haven’t missed a beat, but let’s keep our eyes open for the first signs of wind shifting. Stay close to home, and trust only the voices you’ve known the longest."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels heavier, but the storm hasn’t broken—yet. The old guard is holding, but the cracks are there, and everyone’s watching to see who blinks first. Keep your eyes open, your words light, and your plans ready, just in case."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels different—like the ice is thinning underfoot. Even the most cautious are stepping out, and the old rules no longer hold. Stay sharp, but don’t be surprised if the ground shifts soon."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like the quiet before a storm, not the calm after one. The walls are still standing, but the foundation is shifting beneath them, and no one knows which way it’ll tilt next."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels different—small signs of strain beneath the surface, but nothing yet that breaks the routine. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps careful; the ground may shift, but not today."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
